setting: the hill on the first morning of may after the second of two nights, a hedge full of birds and one of them very close to the microphone, his voice flat and slow with the vowels going long, a stop halfway down where he says nothing for four seconds and then picks up the same sentence, a car door somewhere below

the walk down at twenty past eight after the fourth night in a row, wind flat across the phone, his breathing audible between sentences, two long silences, the second one eleven seconds, a bin lorry braking at the bottom, the last thing he says trailing off into the word anyway

her kitchen on the friday the pile went in, a chair pushed back, the tap running and stopping, the word free said four times and each time faster, a folder dropped flat on the table halfway through, her voice up at the end of every sentence as if still checking something

the hill on the last morning of a four night run with the exam a day away, slower steps than usual, the word paper said eight times and the word exam not at all, a long pause at a gate, a bus pulling out behind him, one sentence started and left where it was

her back step at half nine on a warm half term evening, swifts going over high and thin, a train two streets away, her voice low and unhurried for once with long gaps she does not fill, a mug set down on stone near the end
